pr_title: rework locking in SslStream to support TLS1.3
pr_body:
The locking code in SslStream was broken for quite a while without us noticing. We bump to it with OpenSSL 1.1.1 and TLS1.3 but the fix was to add locking to PAL: https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/pull/37736. I run to the same problems when working on #1720. When MessageDecrypt decides to start renegotiation (there is no real renegotiation in TLS1.3 but on Windows, we still do get  SEC_I_RENEGOTIATE as we need to pass data to `lsass` process. 

I started to fix it but after chatting with @stephentoub we decided to go with a simplistic approach: We grab synchronous lock around DecryptData/EncryptData and if renegotiation is happening we would use create TaskCompletionSource encrypt can wait on for completion. 

With this, the code is pretty simple and old craft can be removed so as the change to OpenSSL PAL. 

Performance seems to be about the same. On Windows, I get results bellow and it changes slightly between runs. On Linux, there was already lock and performance remains the same as well.

issue_context.title: [System.Net.Security] Potential bug in SslStream.Implementation.cs
issue_context.body:
Discovered while annotating the library #32541.

It looks like the `lazyResult` value will never get initialized in this [snippet](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d76ef042f8ead9d06a447ab2b1004ae626185ca2/src/libraries/System.Net.Security/src/System/Net/Security/SslStream.Implementation.cs#L429-L443). Similarly [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d76ef042f8ead9d06a447ab2b1004ae626185ca2/src/libraries/System.Net.Security/src/System/Net/Security/SslStream.Implementation.cs#L510-L524).
comments: I believe @wfurt is already aware of this and working in it.
I'm running final benchmarks and stress on possible fix.  It should be ready today or tomorrow.

review_comments: It'd be helpful to add a comment somewhere detailing the locking scheme being used.  That will, for example, help to explain why it's ok for this nulling out of the field to be done (e.g. because there's only ever one reader at a time, and the reader is responsible for initiating all renegotations, and thus for creating, completing, and removing a waiter).
updated. I added long comment to where the waiter is created and the logic starts.

What happens if below we end up not calling ReplyOnReAuthenticationAsync, e.g. because AllowRenegotation is false?  That will leave _handshakeWaiter as non-null, but no one will ever complete it.  Is that going to cause problems?  Can we ensure that if this is set, it'll always be completed/removed?
I missed that. Since throw, it may not matter but it is cleaner to deal with it explicitly. fixed.

I love that all of this gets deleted.

One step closer to removing LazyAsyncResult entirely :)
I must be missing it... where is _handshakeWaiter completed? i.e. where is {Try}SetResult called?

It seems like I broke it in the final cleanup ;(

This is set in ReplyOnReAuthenticationAsync() now.

The sequence is:

1.  we try to decrypt under lock. 
2. if renegotiation is requested we create TaskCompletionSource still under lock. 
3. that gets cleaned up when a renegotiation is finished. 

4. On write side, we either win and there is no contention and waiting.
5. We get there when a renegotiation is pending. We wait (possibly in loop) until renegotiation is completed as there is no guarantee there is only one. However, in n practice, that is the case so we should be able to finish write/encrypt  as soon as TaskCompletionSource is triggered.
6. Thre are weird cases that renegotiation in TLS1.3 can finish without IO e.g. we get a frame to update session. That needs to be processed but it can finish very quickly. In that case, _handshakeWaiter should be null even if Encrypt failed with TryAgin under lock.
